question.problem:
$$ \{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)={x}^{2}(t)-{y}^{2}(t)+3x(t)+2y(t)-1 \\ {y}^{′}(t)={x}^{2}(t)+y(t)-4x(t)+4\end{aligned} $$ Consider the system of differential equations above. What is the corresponding linearized system at the equilibrium point ${x}^{∗}=[1,\text{ }-1]^{T}?$
${u}^{′}=\,\,$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}} $\,\,u,\,$ where $u=x-{x}^{∗}$
{{field-3}} {{field-4}}
question.worked_solution:
The system can be rewritten in matrix form as 

$$
{x}^{′}=\text{\boldsymbol}f(x)
$$

where $x=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]$ and 
$\text{\boldsymbol}f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+3x+2y-1 \\ {x}^{2}+y-4x+4\end{aligned}].$

We need to compute the Jacobian matrix (or the total derivative) of $\text{\boldsymbol}f(x).$ 

In our case, we have the following:

$$
\text{\boldsymbol}{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+3x+2y-1)=2x+3,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+3x+2y-1)=-2y+2 \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+y-4x+4)=2x-4,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+y-4x+4)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we have

$$
\text{\boldsymbol}{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}2x+3 & -2y+2 \\ 2x-4 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ to get

$$
\text{\boldsymbol}{f}^{′}({x}^{∗})=[\begin{aligned}2(1)+3 & -2(-1)+2 \\ 2(1)-4 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, near the equilibrium, the nonlinear system is approximated by

$$
{u}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]u,
$$

where the deviation vector is

$$
u=x-{x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}x-1 \\ y+1\end{aligned}].
$$
